title: How to flag an email in Apple Mail on Mac: steps, Flagged mailbox, unflagging
metaTitle: How to Flag an Email in Apple Mail on Mac (Step by Step)
description: Learn how to flag an email in Apple Mail on Mac: select the message, click Flag in the toolbar, choose a color, and clear it later.

intro: To flag an email in Apple Mail on Mac, select the message, click the Flag button in the Mail toolbar, and choose a flag. The flag shows in the message header, and the message also appears in the Flagged mailbox when Mail shows that list.
tldr: Select the message, click Flag in the Mail toolbar, and choose a flag.
The flag shows in the message header. The message stays in its mailbox.
Click Flag and choose Clear Flag to remove it.
The Flagged mailbox appears in the sidebar only when more than one flag is in use.
Apple's Mac Mail shortcut list has no flag entry, so use the toolbar.

blocks.text: A flag is a colored marker you put on an email. It tells you the message needs attention later. Flagging does not move the message. It stays in its mailbox, so your Inbox, a folder, or Sent still shows it. A flag only helps if you come back to it. So this page gives you the steps first, then where flags show up, how to clear them, and what to do when something looks wrong.
Flag one message or several at once

Click a message in the list to select it. To flag several messages, hold ⌘ and click each one. To select a run of messages in a row, click the first one, then hold ⇧ and click the last one. Then click the Flag button in the Mail toolbar and choose a flag. Mail applies the flag to every selected message in one action.

Check the result before you move on. Open the message and look at its header, where the flag shows. If nothing changed, the message was probably not selected. Click it once so the highlight shows, then repeat the Flag step. That fixes most cases where a flag seems to fail.

Selection matters more than most people expect. Flag acts on whatever is highlighted, not on whatever your cursor touched last. If three messages are highlighted and you click Flag, all three get the flag. A common mistake is to click one message, scroll, and then flag a different group that is still selected. Look at the highlight first.
Choose a flag and understand the Flagged mailbox

When you click Flag, the menu lists flag colors. Apple's guide uses Red as its example, so look for that color first. A third-party vendor, Canary Mail, says Mail on Mac has seven fixed colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, and gray. Apple's guide does not confirm that count. Open the menu on your own Mac and count them.

The Flagged mailbox does not always appear. Mail shows it in the sidebar only when more than one flag is in use. Flag one message in red, and you will see no Flagged mailbox. Flag a second message in another color, and the mailbox shows up. This catches people out, and it is the first thing to check when Flagged seems to be missing.

Here is a worked example. On Monday you flag a contract in red. The sidebar shows no Flagged item, which looks like a failure but is not. On Tuesday you flag a vendor invoice in a second color. Flagged now appears, with both messages inside it. Click Flagged to see them together, then clear each flag as you finish the task.

items: A flag shows in the message header.
The message stays in its original mailbox.
Flagged appears in the sidebar only when more than one flag is in use.
Clear Flag removes the flag. It does not delete the message.

blocks.text: Clear a flag when the task is done

Select the flagged message, click the Flag button, and choose Clear Flag. The flag comes off, and the message leaves the Flagged list. Clear flags as each task ends. A list of flags that never clear turns into a second inbox, and that defeats the point.

Clearing works on several messages at once. Select them all, click Flag, and choose Clear Flag. Mail applies the change to every selected message. Then check the Flagged mailbox, which should now show fewer messages. If one stays, click it once and repeat the step.

Be careful with the selection when you clear. Clear Flag acts on whatever is highlighted, the same as Flag does. Check the highlight first. Clearing a flag on the wrong message is easy to miss. If a flag seems to have vanished, look in the mailbox where the message lives, then check whether Clear Flag was chosen by mistake.
Rename a flag so it says what you mean

Renaming changes the label, not the color. Apple's example renames Red to Urgent, which is a good model for your own set. Expand Flagged in the sidebar with its disclosure triangle. Click the flag name, click it again, and type the new name. Then press Return to save it.
Good names say what the flag means to you. Waiting on reply, Pay this week, and Read tonight all work. Keep the set short. Three names you use every day beat ten you never check.
Names also help when someone else uses your Mac. A label like Urgent tells them more than a color alone. Pick names that you would understand a week from now, without the message in front of you.
Find every flagged email in one place

Click Flagged in the sidebar to see every flagged message in one list. The messages stay in their own mailboxes. Flagged is a view, not a folder you move mail into. Clear flags from inside Flagged the same way you do anywhere else, with Flag and Clear Flag.

If Flagged is missing, you are using only one flag. Flag a message in a second color, and the mailbox comes back. Keep this in mind when you show a colleague how flags work. They may look for a mailbox that does not appear yet.

Use Flagged as a to-do list for mail. Work from the top, open each message, reply or file it, then clear its flag. The list gets shorter as you go. If it keeps growing, flag fewer messages each morning and be stricter about what counts.
A week of flags, worked through

Monday starts with a full Inbox. You flag three messages in red: a quote that needs a reply, a form to sign, and a question from your manager. The sidebar shows no Flagged item, because only one flag is in use. That is expected.

Tuesday you flag an invoice in a second color. Flagged appears in the sidebar. You open it and see four messages in one list. You reply to two, file one, and clear the flag on each as you finish. Flagged now holds two messages.

Wednesday you rename the red flag to Waiting on reply. The label is clearer than the color alone. Your list reads the same way, but you can scan it faster. You clear the signed form and the reply you sent, and select both before you click Flag so the change applies to both.

Thursday you notice a flag is missing from a message you wanted to keep track of. You look in its mailbox, find the message, and see that Clear Flag was chosen on a selection that included it. You flag it again and move on.

Friday you clear everything left in Flagged. The sidebar item may disappear again, because only one flag remains in use, or the list may be empty. Either result is fine. The week's flags did their job.
Flag from iCloud.com and check the shortcut

On iCloud.com, you flag from the web app, not from the Mac app. Select a message, or hold Command and click several. Then click Mark, or the More button, and choose Flag. Flagged messages show a flag icon in the list. For one message in an open conversation, use the More button in the bottom-right corner, then Flag.

Apple's page does not explain how to clear a flag on iCloud.com. If you cannot find a clear action there, use the Mac app, where Apple's steps are documented. Flags you set in one app should still appear when you check the same account elsewhere, though sync can lag.

Apple's iCloud.com shortcut table lists Shift-Command-L for flagging. That table covers the web app. Apple's Mac Mail shortcut table has no flag entry, and the only related entry is Shift-Command-U, which marks a message read or unread. Some third-party guides say Shift-Command-L also works in Mac Mail. Apple does not confirm that. Test it on a selected message. If nothing happens, use the toolbar.

items: Flagging with nothing selected. Click the message so it highlights, then click Flag.
Expecting the Flagged mailbox after one flag. Mail shows it only when more than one flag is in use.
Mixing up flags with read status. Mark as read or unread uses Shift-Command-U, a separate action.
Thinking a flag moves the message. It stays in its mailbox and also appears in Flagged.
Expecting every device to match. Community reports describe Gmail flags not syncing across devices. Apple does not document this.

blocks.text: If flags do not sync, check the account first. Community suggestions include rebuilding the mailbox or re-adding the account. Apple's flag guide does not cover either fix, so read Apple's Mail account steps before you change anything. Re-adding an account changes its settings, so note your account details first.
Build a daily flagging routine

Flags work best inside a routine. Each morning, scan the Inbox and flag mail that needs a reply that day. Around midday, open Flagged and work through it. Before you log off, clear the flags on anything you finished. The flags left over tell you what carries into tomorrow.

Email takes a large share of the workday. McKinsey research from 2012 put email at 28% of the workweek, about 11.2 hours, for the average knowledge worker. That figure reaches this page through Clean Email, not McKinsey's own report, so treat it as a rough guide.

Apple Mail accounts for a large share of email opens. Litmus counts it at 76.56% in its September 2026 report. That count includes Mail Privacy Protection opens, which do not reliably show the app or platform, so read it as a rough share.

A Microsoft study from April 2025 found workers spent over 11 hours a week on email before Copilot. Copilot users saved nearly 3 hours a week, about 25%. These numbers measure email time in general. No source I checked measures how people use flags.

Related Mail tasks to set up next

Once flags make sense, sorting comes next. [Create a rule to sort incoming mail in Apple Mail on Mac](/how-to/create-a-rule-to-sort-incoming-mail-in-apple-mail) can sort mail as it arrives. If a few senders matter most, [use the VIP mailbox in Apple Mail on Mac](/how-to/use-the-vip-mailbox-in-apple-mail) keeps them in one place. To find everything from one person, [search emails by sender in Apple Mail on Mac](/how-to/search-emails-by-sender-in-apple-mail). For the app itself, see [AI assistant for Apple Mail](/apps/apple-mail).
Check your Mail version before you follow the menu

Apple's flag guide does not name the macOS or Mail version it covers, and this page does not either. The steps follow that guide and the Flag button in the toolbar. If your toolbar looks different, look for a flag control in the toolbar and in the Message menu. Some guides list Message > Flag > Toggle Flag. Apple does not confirm that path, so check your own Message menu before you rely on it.

faq.question: Can I flag several emails at once in Apple Mail?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold ⌘ and click each message, or click one and hold ⇧ to select a range. Then click Flag in the toolbar and choose a flag. The flag applies to every selected message.

faq.question: Why can't I see the Flagged mailbox?
faq.answer: Mail shows the Flagged mailbox only when more than one flag is in use. Flag a second message in another color, and the mailbox appears in the sidebar.

faq.question: How do I remove a flag from an email?
faq.answer: Select the message, click Flag in the toolbar, and choose Clear Flag. The message stays in its mailbox, and it leaves the Flagged list.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to flag an email in Mail on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's Mac Mail shortcut list has no flag entry. Apple lists Shift-Command-L for flagging on iCloud.com, which is the web app. Press it on a selected message to test it, and use the toolbar if nothing happens.

faq.question: Does flagging move the email to another folder?
faq.answer: No. A flagged message stays in its original mailbox and also appears in the Flagged mailbox when Mail shows that list.

faq.question: Can I rename a flag in Apple Mail?
faq.answer: Yes. Expand Flagged in the sidebar, click the flag name, click it again, and type a new name. Apple's example renames Red to Urgent.

faq.question: Can Lazur flag the email for me?
faq.answer: Lazur does not click buttons for you. Ask where the Flag button is, and Lazur circles it on your screen and explains what it does. For a full walkthrough, ask Lazur to guide you one click at a time.

steps.name: Select the message
steps.text: In the message list, click the email you want to flag. To flag several, hold ⌘ and click each one. The highlight shows what is selected.
steps.tip: Flag acts on whatever is highlighted, so check the highlight before you click Flag.

steps.name: Click the Flag button
steps.text: Look at the Mail toolbar at the top of the window, then click Flag. Apple's guide places the button in the Mail toolbar.
steps.tip: If the button is hard to spot, make sure Mail is the front window and a message is selected.

steps.name: Choose a flag
steps.text: Pick a flag color from the menu. Apple's guide uses Red as its example. Mail applies the flag to every selected message.
steps.tip: A third-party vendor says Mail has seven colors. Count them on your own Mac.

steps.name: Check the header and sidebar
steps.text: Look at the message header, where the flag shows. If the sidebar shows Flagged, click it to see every flagged message in one list.
steps.tip: Flagged appears only when more than one flag is in use.

steps.name: Clear the flag when you finish
steps.text: Select the message, click Flag, and choose Clear Flag. The flag comes off, and the message stays in its mailbox.
steps.tip: Clear flags as you finish each task, so Flagged stays short.

steps.name: Rename a flag (optional)
steps.text: Click the disclosure triangle next to Flagged in the sidebar. Click the flag name, click it again, and type a new name. Apple's example renames Red to Urgent.
steps.tip: Short names are easier to scan.

steps.name: Test the shortcut (optional)
steps.text: Apple's Mac Mail shortcut list has no flag entry. Press ⇧⌘L on a selected message. If nothing happens, keep using the toolbar.
steps.tip: Apple lists ⇧⌘L for flagging on iCloud.com, so test before you rely on it.

troubleshooting.problem: The Flag button is missing from the toolbar.
troubleshooting.fix: Make sure a message is selected and the Mail window is the front window. Apple's guide places Flag in the Mail toolbar, so check that the toolbar is showing.

troubleshooting.problem: The Flagged mailbox does not appear in the sidebar.
troubleshooting.fix: Mail shows it only when more than one flag is in use. Flag a second message in another color, and the mailbox should appear.

troubleshooting.problem: A flag seems to have disappeared.
troubleshooting.fix: Flagging does not move a message. Look in the mailbox where the email lives, and check whether Clear Flag was chosen by mistake on a selection.

troubleshooting.problem: Flags do not match on another device.
troubleshooting.fix: Community reports describe Gmail flags not syncing. Apple does not document a fix. Check the account in Mail first, and treat rebuilding the mailbox or re-adding the account as community suggestions.
